features.evidence: Bachelor's, Master's, or Doctoral degree in computer science
features.name: advanced degree attainment
features.description: Captures how far the applicant's formal academic preparation matches the role's preferred graduate-level background.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent only.
Master's degree in computer science or a related field.
Doctoral degree in computer science or a related field.

features.evidence: 3, 5, or 7 years launching 2, 4, or 6 production services
features.name: depth of shipped software experience
features.description: Captures the extent of hands-on professional experience testing, maintaining, launching, and operating production backend systems.

levels.descriptor: Meets the minimum with roughly 2 to 3 years of experience and limited evidence of repeated service launches.
Shows solid mid-level experience, typically 3 to 5 years and several production services owned or launched.
Shows extensive experience, typically 5 to 7 or more years with repeated launches and sustained ownership across multiple services.

features.evidence: Python is all over my recent work
features.name: Python production fluency
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter shows Python as a serious working language for services, automation, or tooling relevant to the role.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful Python experience is mentioned.
Python is mentioned mainly for scripts or light tooling.
Python is shown as a regular production language for services, tooling, or automation.
Python is presented as production-grade or central to important internal systems and automation.

features.evidence: shipping LLM-backed features and hardening them against unpredictable inputs
features.name: AI production hardening
features.description: Captures experience applying AI systems in production, especially with attention to evaluation, trustworthiness, and failure modes.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
AI or LLM work is mentioned only broadly, without clear production evidence.
The letter shows production experience shipping model-backed features.
The letter shows production AI experience plus explicit evaluation, hardening, or trustworthiness practices.

features.evidence: Python agents supervised by Go services that log and constrain every step
features.name: agentic tooling architecture
features.description: Captures direct design ownership of agent-based systems, especially the structure, guardrails, and division between agents and backend control planes.

levels.descriptor: No agentic tooling experience is mentioned.
Agents are mentioned vaguely, with little sense of ownership or design.
The applicant says they designed agentic systems end to end.
The applicant explains bounded autonomy, auditability, permissions, or a clear Go and Python control architecture.

features.evidence: deduplicating findings and routing them to the owning teams
features.name: vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Captures whether the applicant has already automated vulnerability intake, classification, deduplication, routing, or similar security-response workflows.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability-handling automation is mentioned.
The applicant talks about wanting to automate security work but gives no direct example.
The applicant says they built vulnerability-report or triage automation.
The applicant describes concrete workflow elements or impact such as classification, deduplication, routing, self-serve handling, or time saved.

features.evidence: threat modeling and code review for common vulnerability classes
features.name: security assessment practice
features.description: Captures direct experience performing security assessments rather than only building general backend software.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment experience is mentioned.
Security review exposure is implied but vague.
The letter gives concrete assessment work such as threat models, code review, or service reviews.
The letter shows formal or structured assessments with remediation follow-through or an explicitly attacker-minded approach.

features.evidence: turned a brute-force correlation job into a streaming computation
features.name: algorithmic problem solving
features.description: Captures the strength and recency of the applicant's data-structures and algorithms ability as shown through concrete engineering examples.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic evidence is given.
The applicant claims comfort with algorithms or data structures but gives no meaningful example.
The applicant gives one concrete redesign, optimization, or data-structure choice example.
The applicant presents a strong algorithmic foundation with a substantive, high-impact example.

features.name: formal security credential
features.description: Captures whether the letter offers an external security credential, and how practice-oriented that credential is.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A foundational credential such as Security+ is mentioned.
A hands-on offensive credential such as OSCP is mentioned.

features.evidence: placed near the top of several well-attended competitions
features.name: offensive practice through CTF
features.description: Captures ongoing exposure to attacker thinking through capture-the-flag or similar competitive security practice.

levels.descriptor: No offensive practice is mentioned.
The applicant mentions occasional CTF participation.
The applicant shows regular CTF participation as continuing practice.
The applicant signals serious competitive involvement or strong CTF results.

features.evidence: writing the patch and sending it upstream
features.name: open-source ownership
features.description: Captures how much the applicant demonstrates public maintenance, upstream contribution, or responsibility for software used by others.

levels.descriptor: No open-source activity is mentioned.
The applicant mentions occasional upstream patches.
The applicant maintains a small project or is a recurring contributor.
The applicant maintains a library or framework with outside users, reviews, and releases.

features.evidence: distributed job scheduler with leader election and crash recovery
features.name: personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition and relevance of the applicant's self-directed engineering work outside their day job.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
A small utility or app is mentioned, with limited systems depth.
A substantial standalone engineering project is described.
A complex distributed or reliability-focused system is described, built to explore hard failure modes or systems tradeoffs.

features.evidence: making secure development the default rather than the exception
features.name: secure by default philosophy
features.description: Captures how strongly the applicant articulates the role as embedding protections into everyday development rather than adding after-the-fact process.

levels.descriptor: No clear secure-by-default idea appears.
The letter shows generic interest in security impact.
The applicant explicitly wants to embed security into the development lifecycle or reduce manual security burden.
The applicant states a clear philosophy about defaults, lifecycle integration, or security as engineering rather than compliance.

features.evidence: improvements there are inherited by every team downstream
features.name: platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures motivation for foundational work whose benefits compound across many teams, products, or users.

levels.descriptor: No platform-scale motivation is shown.
Scale or impact is mentioned only in passing.
The applicant clearly values foundational systems that help many teams.
The applicant vividly frames broad organizational leverage as a core reason for applying.

features.evidence: too many signals, too few experts
features.name: security automation problem framing
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter identifies the underlying security-operations bottleneck the role is meant to solve.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not frame the problem beyond wanting the role.
Automation is discussed only abstractly.
The letter identifies a concrete bottleneck such as manual triage or overloaded experts.
The letter frames the work as a specific systems problem and links automation to capacity gains, variant analysis, or routine response.

features.evidence: classification and routing layer that lets engineers spend their attention on fixes
features.name: specificity of evidence
features.description: Captures whether claims are backed by concrete mechanisms, outcomes, or examples rather than generic alignment language.

levels.descriptor: Mostly generic claims or restated job language, with little concrete evidence.
Some concrete examples appear, but detail and outcome are limited.
Multiple specific examples are given, with technical mechanism or task detail.
The letter is consistently specific, using architecture choices, outcomes, or clear operational impact to substantiate claims.

features.evidence: Engnieer, tht, drwas versus clean prose
features.name: writing polish
features.description: Captures the mechanical professionalism of the letter, especially typo frequency and whether errors distract from credibility.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors noticeably distract and undermine polish.
Several errors are present, but the letter remains readable.
Only minor errors are present.
The letter is clean and professional throughout.
